summary: ToolRuntime registers scoped tools; defineTool validates arguments and canonical output, and pure render projects the value for model content.
A dsh.bundle patch can mount an installable tool plugin in a named Profile through the dsh plugin CLI.
Bundle patch paths and named Profile bundle selection compose an ordered plugin tree through the published dsh CLI.
Cordis Context plugins declare injected services, provide fiber-owned services and effects, and expose awaitable fiber startup and disposal.
TimerService mixes fiber-owned timeout, interval, throttle and debounce into Context; legacy setTimeout/setInterval are deprecated.
Loader imports configured plugin rows, Include applies ordered detached patches and file-backed trees, and Group nests child rows under DSH Host builtins.
A later Profile patch can disable an existing plugin row and insert a cordis:group carrying the same installed plugin as a nested row.
The glossary distinguishes Host plugin fibers, services, bundles, Profiles, Loader entries and canonical tool results using target-source ownership boundaries.
DSH base Profile owns an HMR service with config-only default; enabled module roots and profile patch watches enter one serialized queue.
Web Client HMR has a Host stat-poll and SSE transport plus browser entry reconciliation through Client Modules.
Host Typert Remote declarations require generated descriptors and explicit Client assembly selection; Gateway dispatches through Connection with typed RemoteResult failures.
Session append accepts lossless event facts while only supported surface events and registered message projections contribute model-visible history.
Persistence service and handle separate append visibility, writer ownership and flush durability; read handles are independent of the writer lease.
Agent loop owns persistent write handles for Agent sessions and closes interrupted turns on resume after obtaining write ownership.
Plugin event facts can be folded by event type and sequence; crash durability requires the owner persistence flush and restoration of the same interpreter.

A web Client half attaches to a bare package Loader row with dsh.client.platform web and an exported built ./client registration factory; its graph and browser fiber are distinct from Host installation.
Independent Client plugin packages must publish a lazy factory script satisfying the public registration protocol; the repository-local clientBundle build preset is not a published package API.

PluginManager reads and changes current Profile rows and bundle selections, returning persisted-change and runtime-application outcomes separately; cancellation and failed operations can leave partial state requiring readback.
The plugin_manager model tool checks permission escalation for each action, while build-script and exact-version compatibility approvals are separate decisions.

A custom Remote task composes Host Remote service declaration, generated Typert descriptors, explicit Client contribution assembly, Host gateway and Client call; the draft task still requires independent generated declaration and browser verification.
Installing and changing a bundle requires a published patch, Profile package operation, readback of saved selection and Loader rows, and an actual runtime observation after restart when required.

A minimal independent Client package publishes a Host entry, Web manifest, bare-name patch row and registration factory; a Web Profile and browser observation are required to confirm activation and cleanup.
Client slot declarations define cardinality and scope; SlotRegistry registration and inject contributions are owned by caller fiber and disposed with parent declarations.
Client resources route address protocols to a single provider, hold one stream while subscribers or pins exist, and abort it when the last holder leaves.
Credential refs resolve layered env-name values while owner-scoped record keys use explicit record operations; local provider validates file permissions and commits before update events.
Authorization flows have unique owner keys, one attempt per key, cancellation and prompt outcomes, and only report authorized after observing a credential record commit.
A Host bundle can register a scoped authorization flow, prompt for a secret and commit a record, then verify saved state and cleanup in a real Profile.
SettingsForms edits volatile Config fields through validated JSON and revision checks; Client wire reads are redacted while Host describe can be unredacted.
Permission preset selection records intent in Session and applies sandbox and approval knobs through their owning setters; custom is derived and auto requires a fixed live integration.

A plugin should separate secret references or record ownership, editable settings and execution permission selection when those capabilities are needed; the combined task is a draft pending independent consumer validation.
SessionQueryEngine offers trusted exact reads and optional SQLite search; search index is derived, openAt never disables search, and direct service calls do not authorize callers.
To give Agent history search, explicitly enable a SQLite FTS index and mount the optional session query model tool; confirm exact cwd authorization and real Profile behavior.
SubagentRuntime registers named Providers and separates prepublication cleanup from caller-owned runs, while continuable children require distinct durable identity and inbox handling.
ACP subprocess Provider advertises no optional one-shot capabilities, has no continuable creation, and owns child process startup and teardown for each run.
Tool adapter mounts model-visible delegation only while its selected Provider exists, validates capability and depth settings, and releases foreground one-shot runs after result.
A Profile can combine the subprocess ACP Provider with a model tool using provider-managed depth and a separately configured child ACP server, subject to real handshake verification.
LlmRuntime binds provider routes atomically to adapters, keeps catalog and prepared call generation separate, and consumes ordered streaming chunks and explicit failure reasons.
An independent Host bundle can register a route and model catalog, emit canonical chunks and clean up its registration; the fixed-text fixture refuses real Agent requests.
Agent model selection snapshots a route for prompt assembly and request headers, while Session Controller validates catalog membership and records selection intent in Session events.
A selectable adapter needs a current model catalog and Session Controller call, followed by actual Agent request and replay checks; the fixed-text fixture is insufficient for that end-to-end test.
Inspect the final Profile hmr row, apply owned patch and module changes, and check old fiber disposal and new behavior; module replacement remains unverified in this run.
Rebuild an installed Client bundle, observe rebuilt graph delivery and browser fiber replacement, then verify disposal; real rebuild replacement remains unverified in this run.
Session projection folds committed Session events into registered state and optional wire views; cache is derived and version-bound.
A Host plugin can register a pure projection and validate append/snapshot behavior; cache cold restore and Profile unload are still unverified.
Storage hub selects a Backend; domain KV serializes durable writes before memory update and emits post-commit domain/changed.
A Host plugin can mount JSON Backend and typed domain KV, then verify close/reopen, update, delete, and event order; SQLite remains separately unverified.
WebServer owns first exact and then prefix HTTP/upgrade routes, a single fallback seat, index taps, and fiber scoped registration; raw handlers own method/body/response.
Host Connection supplies admitted /api request waterfall and Fetch/RPC seats; Client service owns generation and recovery observations.
A Web Profile plugin can register a route and call Connection admission before responding; isolated published-package smoke covered auth, request rejection, and fiber unload.
Jobs service defines owner scoped producer registration and output, while jobs-local implements process-local execution and tool-jobs exposes model controls.
Schedule service persists exact-Session tasks, delivers due work to Agent and flushes Session before task advancement; enqueue and task write are not atomic.
Plan mode records immediate or next-step transitions; Todo tool writes complete list snapshots and projection clears at the next turn start.
External SDK client owns a same-version CLI child process and JSON-RPC session lifecycle; server and protocol packages are composition dependencies.
An independent TypeScript caller can initialize, run and close an SDK session; isolated fake peer smoke covered handshake and event flow, not model/Profile behavior.
MCP client instances own one server namespace, scoped discovered tools and optional resources; fiber disposal removes registrations.
A Host Profile can mount a named MCP server and inspect tool/resource registrations and cleanup; isolated stdio discovery passed while HTTP and reconnect remain unverified.
A Session-owned producer can return a Job id, expose output to model tools and cancel; isolated runtime completed and killed jobs, while Profile model turn remains untested.
A Host Profile can add Schedule, create a future exact-Session task and delete it; isolated Cordis runtime and Profile boot passed, due delivery/restart remain untested.
Client ConfigForms mirrors Host Settings describe and stages revision-fenced writes; form save can partially succeed across config and secret writes.
An external Client bundle can expose a Host volatile Config through a keyed plugins.row.config card with a lazy CJS factory; independent Host/Client compile and bundle registration passed.
Built-in Web UI separates future-Session default permission preset from current-Session /permission choice; Profile/browser persistence remains unverified.
FileSystem seam owns opaque targets, observations and write/edit intents; an ordered observation policy enforces first-intent decisions.
A Host listener placed before default observation policy can deny write/edit intent for an owned readonly tree; isolated published-package smoke observed FS_PERMISSION_DENIED.
Shell service resolves and executes through a selected Provider; bash-local is a local subprocess executor and does not itself add sandbox confinement.
A Host plugin can register a fixed command tool against ctx.shell; isolated published-package smoke observed exit 0 and scoped removal, not ToolRuntime permission dispatch.
SkillRegistry registers scoped providers and definitions, with asynchronous list/get, invalidate and fiber-owned cleanup.
A Host plugin can register an owned provider and verify list/get and disposal; isolated Cordis service smoke passed, Agent Skill invocation was not run.
SystemPrompt owns ordered sections, runtime context, variables and assembly hooks; direct render does not persist a Session snapshot.
A Host plugin can register section and context contributions with fiber cleanup; isolated service render passed while AgentLoop Session persistence remains unverified.
GoalService binds exact live Agent goals to committed goal/change events and revision CAS; round driver and model tools have separate authority.
A trusted Host caller can create/pause a Goal with revision CAS; isolated real Goal service observed two committed events, not Agent continuation.
WorkflowEngine returns a holder-owned run with nonrejecting result and explicit disposal; Agent loop factory create/resume is a separate composition boundary.
A trusted Host caller can await and release a WorkflowRun; isolated fixture used a stub engine and did not execute PTC.
ToolRuntime runs pre, guard, around, post and result hooks with scoped disposers; guard denial is monotonic and result observation is readonly.
ApprovalService requires an open Agent turn, records asked/decided outcomes and fails closed on missing or aborted answerer.
A Host plugin can combine pre-execute ask, guard denial and result observation; isolated service smoke covered short calls, guard and missing-Agent denial, not an allowed-once answer.
An independent Client bundle can show a resource first frame in a Session header slot; real Web Profile and Chrome observed abort/reopen and online unload cleanup.
Conversation Node definitions project Session events to view nodes; Chat routes kind to keyed renderer slots with fiber scoped registration.
An independent Client bundle can project turn/start to a keyed Chat node; real Web Profile and Chrome observed visible text after disclosure expansion and online removal cleanup.
